messages:
incidentbot: PagerDuty alert fired: INCIDENT #PD-4821 -> gpu-host-rt14-node49 kernel_panic (kubelet not ready)

pagerduty: AUTOPAGE -> escalation to oncall-dev (Sara) and oncall-backup (Mike). See: https://pd.internal/PD-4821

Sara (dev-oncall): acked. I'm attaching serial console and checking node status. @Devon can you pull nvme logs for rt14-node49?

Mike (dev-oncall): I'm looking at cluster autoscaler, traffic routing. Early signs: node lost heartbeat, kubelet in CrashLoopBackOff after kernel oops.

Devon (infra): pulling dmesg & nvme SMART from node49 now. Saw a cascade of `nvme error` then `kernel panic - stack trace`. Possible NVMe firmware flake.

Jin (platform-sre): FYI control-plane shows pods moved, but some Dedicated inference pools (dedicated-rt14) have reduced capacity. Routing fallback to ded-spot-2 triggered. Impact: 1.6% of requests returned 503s in last 2m, mostly from customer ACME (dedicated namespace acme-prod).

Support Ops - Maya: Customer ACME reported latency spikes and a few 500s. I've opened ticket ACME-7321 and escalated to their SRE. Sharing logs.

Sara (dev-oncall): Plan: cordon node -> drain safe -> reroute traffic -> attempt reboot & serial capture -> if NVMe errors persist, kick RMA. Anyone object to draining immediately?

Mike (dev-oncall): go for drain. Runbook: <https://runbook.internal/infra/gpu-node-failure|gpu-node-failure> step 3. Use `kubectl drain rt14-node49 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then reroute.

Devon (infra): ran `kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=rt14-node49` and `journalctl -k -b -1 -u kubelet` snippets show `IOMMU: device reset timed out` then `kernel: general protection fault`. Copying excerpts:
```
[ 1432.678901] nvme0: I/O 0 QID 1 timeout
[ 1432.678904] nvme0: controller reset failed
[ 1432.678910] kernel: kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception
```

Sara (dev-oncall): drain in progress. Will keep pods with persistent volumes evicted per runbook. Starting reroute to eu-fallback and us-east-burst.

Jin (platform-sre): Autoscaler noticed reduced capacity and spun up a new node in us-east. But quantized model pool small-quant-1 started accepting requests; we should monitor quality/regressions. Redwood Optimize flagged potential 2% quality delta for that model variant. Notify product if degradation persists.

Mike (dev-oncall): Drain completed. `kubectl cordon/evict` logs included. Some pods with local NVMe volumes failed to relocate; we're forcing restart of their sidecars.

Support Ops - Maya: Notifying ACME via ACME-7321: we're rerouting to backup pools, will follow up with post-incident summary.

Devon (infra): Reboot attempted via BMC: `ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.10.14.49 -U admin chassis power cycle`. Serial shows kernel panic on boot at `nvme_probe`. Repro on attach. We should RMA drive.

Lee (ops-manager): If RMA needed, raise a hardware-incident ticket and consider reserving replacement in rt14 spares. Also confirm whether Dedicated contract SLAs are triggered.

Sara (dev-oncall): Taking ownership to run a 1hr mitigation timeline: 0-5m drain (done), 5-15m reroute & verify (ongoing), 15-60m attempt controlled reboot & serial capture (in progress), 60m+ escalate RMA if NVMe still failing.

pagerduty: PD escalation: ACKED by Sara at 1777777782. On-call handoff window set to Mike if Sara needs escalation.

incidentbot: automated note: Created internal follow-up task INF-RT14-49 and hardware ticket HW-RMA-974.

Mike (dev-oncall): QA check: error rate dropped to 0.4% after reroute. ACME still seeing intermittent 502s for long requests (>8s). Might be cache warmup / KV cache misses.

Jin (platform-sre): started KV cache warmup script for acme's prefix sets. Also spinning a temporary smaller batch pool to handle long sequence requests.

Devon (infra): collecting SMART with `nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0`; CRC errors and media errors count rising. Confirm RMA.

Sara (dev-oncall): I'm trashing node from rotation after RMA plan. Mike, if I need to hand off, I'll post `handoff:` with checklist.

Mike (dev-oncall): Copy. Standby for handoff.

Support Ops - Maya: Communicating to ACME: we've mitigated impact, lower error rate, escalated hardware RMA, will provide RCA.

Lee (ops-manager): Good containment, please ensure we log the timeline and customer impact percent for billing/credits.

Sara (dev-oncall): handoff: I need to step out for 20m. Actionables for next oncall: monitor ACME-7321, verify RMA ticket HW-RMA-974 progress, confirm KV warmup reduces long-tail 502s, finalize postmortem draft. Passing to Mike.

Mike (dev-oncall): ack takeover at 1777778005. I'll continue monitoring and escalate to infra if node doesn't respond to RMA scheduling.

incidentbot: thread auto-closed for paging updates; keep posting status changes.
